newsitem.title: UK: Punishment beatings on increase in Northern Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Punishment beatings on increase in Northern Ireland.

text.p: The number of punishment beatings by Northern Ireland extremists on both sides of the sectarian divide in the British province have risen sharply this year, the government revealed on Monday.

Irish Republicans were responsible for 158 beatings and Protestant hardliners accounted for 118, Northern Ireland Minister Sir John Wheeler told parliament. This is a rise of 59 on the total for the whole of last year.

Extremists take the law into their own hands by meting out beatings for what they call "anti-social" crimes that range from joyridding to drug peddling. They use everything from concrete blocks to baseball bats to beat their victims.
Wheeler said a typical victim would cost the state 9,000 pounds ($15,160) in legal, medical and policing costs.
